title: Expert Brain Domain root
description: One per <X> Expertise/ folder. Declares the subdomain spine, the id scheme validate.py enforces, and the glossary. Holds no expertise itself.

dir.description: Folder name. Numbered so the lifecycle reads in order on disk.

artifact_kinds.description: The five Atlas knowledge types that are not objects, plus terminology: their folder and id prefix. Documentation for authors; the authoritative mapping lives in vocabulary.yaml closed.artifact_kinds and is what validate.py enforces.

core_artifacts.description: The shared knowledge-artifact roster, grouped by kind. Pinned before authoring so a capability's knowledge.yaml can reference MEDDICC on the day MEDDICC does not exist yet — unauthored entries are tracked through planned_objects rather than reading as dead links.

core_objects.description: The shared library roster, grouped for readability. Every name here must exist as objects/core/<name>.yaml and be loaded by at least two capabilities — validate.py checks both.

planned_objects.description:
Object AND artifact ids that are known to be coming but are not authored yet. A reference to one of these is a WARNING; a reference to an id that appears nowhere is an ERROR.

This is what lets real expertise be authored before the whole library exists. Without it every honest forward reference — 'Decision Maker approves Proposal', 'this capability applies MEDDICC' — becomes a dead link, and a validator that cries wolf three hundred times is a validator nobody runs.

Regenerate with _tools/plan.py; seed it by hand when you are pinning a roster the authoring pass will fill.

scope.description: core, or the capability leaf it is scoped to.

referenced_by.description: How many files already point at it. High counts are the objects to author first.
